description: 470 µF **500 V** snap-in aluminium electrolytic, 105 °C, −40 °C category, 35 mm land (split DC link). The 500 V class is the requirement: at 500 V the worst continuous half is 435 V = 87 % and 86 % at the F.38 (430 V) / F.03 (850 V) limits, while a 450 V part runs 92 % nominal, 96 % at the 860 V OVP and 97.3–97.8 % at the F.38 boundary — above ~90 % of V_R the leakage and oxide-repair rate climb off the datasheet endurance curve. Lowering the bus instead is not available: the 830 V link is SET by the 500 V bank edge with 2.3 % of FHA gain margin (checked at Lr +5 % / Cr −5 % / Lm +7 %), so 810 V and below fail the gain, and capping LOW mode at 480 V pushes 480–500 V into HIGH with a 240–250 V bank. RFQ LINE (binding): height ≤ the drawn can, **ripple ≥ 5.2 A rms @ 100 kHz / 105 °C**, **ESR ≤ 80 mΩ @ 100 kHz**, leakage ≤ 0.5 mA per can at 85 °C/415 V graded/matched per half, endurance lot 1000 h at 438 V/105 °C on 5 samples. THE DUTY THAT LINE IS FOR: the dominant term is the **Vienna's own 50 kHz capacitor current**, not the LLC's 2·f_sw share. At 50 kHz the per-phase commutation films are 3 µF per half (1.06 Ω) against a can bank of 13–16 mΩ, so the cans take essentially all of it. Direct PWM evaluation on the firmware's own modulator (common centred carrier, min-max zero sequence) plus the LLC 2·f_sw share and the 150 Hz neutral-point term in quadrature gives **5.7 / 6.5 / 5.9 A rms per can at 400 VAC / 800 V** and **6.7 / 7.6 / 7.0 A at 340 VAC / 700 V** (30 / 40 / 50 kW, full power — V_FULL is 330 VAC, so 340 VAC is NOT a derated point). An independent switched model with its own film/ESR split reads about 0.6 × the nominal figure, so the two methods bracket the answer and this line is set from the conservative bracket. `current-coordination [DCLINK-VIENNA]` recomputes all of it every run from tanks.mjs, the committed ripple-share CSV and THIS line, and gates the nominal-line corner against it × the ≤ 70 °C ambient multiplier (1.3×). **REGISTERED EXCEEDANCE — the 340 VAC full-power corner runs 99–112 % of that allowance and is the RFQ decision, not a number to widen.** Levers, in order: force air across the bank (the ambient multiplier is worth more than any part change); a taller / larger-diameter 470–680 µF / 500 V long-life can at ≥ 6 A — note the height line above, this is a mechanical decision; +1 can per half (+₹350–400 and a board change). 5.2 A at 105 °C is at the TOP of what a 35 mm snap-in gives. **PRICE RISK, NOT APPLIED:** a long-life ≥ 4.8 A snap-in is above the ₹185 @1k carried here; RFQ round 1 closes it
